name: Anterdipan Singh
thesis_title: Optical Modelling, TCAD Simulation, and Experimental Investigation of ITO/n-MoS2-x/p-Si(c)/p+-Si(Al)/Ag heterojunction Solar cells
abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), particularly molybdenum disulfide (MoS₂₋ₓ), have emerged as promising materials for next-generation silicon heterojunction solar cells owing to their tunable optoelectronic properties, intrinsic n-type conductivity, and favorable band alignment with silicon. This work presents a comprehensive investigation of defect engineering, optical parameter extraction, and physics-based device modeling of ITO/n-MoS₂₋ₓ/p-Si(c)/p⁺-Si(Al)/Ag heterojunction solar cells. A novel approach is developed to extract the refractive index of ultrathin MoS₂₋ₓ films deposited on non-transparent silicon substrates without relying on optical interference fringes. The experimentally derived optical constants are incorporated into TCAD Sentaurus simulations using the transfer-matrix method to investigate light propagation and absorption. Furthermore, a two-defect electrical model is established to distinguish the contributions of sulfur vacancy-induced donor states and recombination centers. To validate the modeling framework, MoS₂₋ₓ thin films with controlled sulfur vacancy concentrations are synthesized using dual-zone chemical vapor deposition and characterized through XPS, Raman, photoluminescence, and electron microscopy. The experimentally extracted material parameters are subsequently integrated into device simulations, demonstrating strong agreement between simulated and measured photovoltaic characteristics. This work establishes an integrated experimental and computational framework for understanding defect-mediated optoelectronic behavior and optimizing MoS₂₋ₓ/Si heterojunction solar cells.
keywords: Silicon heterojunction solar cells;  Defect-based TCAD modeling; Optical constants; Refractive index extraction; Dual-zone chemical vapor deposition (DZCVD); Plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD); Thermal evaporation; RF/DC sputtering; Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation; Transfer-matrix method (TMM).

name: Ameer Suhail
thesis_title: A Scalable Optofluidic Microreactor Platform: Development and Demonstration for Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution, Overall Water Splitting, and Liquid-Phase Alkylation
abstract: Photocatalytic water splitting offers a simple route to green hydrogen, but scaling it up requires reactors that couple catalysts effectively to light, water and product removal. Existing flat panels are hydrodynamically passive, while optofluidic microreactors depend on fabrication routes too costly for large areas. This thesis develops a scalable optofluidic microreactor platform on commercial soda-lime glass, using laser-lithography-assisted wet etching and spray-coated catalyst immobilization with a colloidal-silica binder. The route needs no clean room or photomask, and was extended to large-area plates with a favourable projected cost. The platform was demonstrated in three projects. Immobilized Pt–CdS nanowires gave visible-light hydrogen evolution well above a matched suspension reactor. Al-doped SrTiO₃ achieved overall water splitting without sacrificial reagents in a CFD-guided reactor, with activity strongly governed by flow and bubble removal. A serpentine reactor then performed continuous-flow tert-butylation of phenol, and numbering up plates in parallel increased conversion at unchanged throughput. One fabrication route thus served three different reactions, with the limits in each case traced to identified causes.
keywords: Optofluidic microreactor; Photocatalytic water splitting; Hydrogen evolution; Overall water splitting; Laser-lithography-assisted wet etching; Spray coating; Computational fluid dynamics; tert-Butylation of phenol; Continuous-flow chemistry; Scalable fabrication

name: Rishabh Mahanta
thesis_title: Efficient Management of Intermittently Powered systems for forward progress of applications
abstract:
Intermittent computing systems (ImC) are a product of evolving edge devices. ImC is envisioned as a possible substitute for devices with consistent power and battery backup. The need for creative architectural designs has resulted from the difficulties of unreliable power-supply, which causes frequent interruptions in task execution, prevent the widespread deployment of such systems. 

Our work proposes newer architectures for ImC that uses a volatile SRAM cache to minimize runtime interruptions and speed up task execution. There are speed and energy benefits to faster writing to SRAM caches. Frequently written blocks are stored on a tiny STT scratchpad memory in case of evictions. 
   
However, as these systems lack active cooling mechanisms, elevated on-chip temperatures lead to significant leakage in volatile components such as SRAM caches, resulting in severe energy loss and reduced reliability, especially in environments where the power supply is constant and the ambient temperature is high. We design a temperature-aware and energy-efficient architecture for ImC systems that dynamically mitigates thermal-induced leakage. Implemented on the GEM5 simulator and analyzed using McPAT, NVSim, CACTI, and HotSpot. The results demonstrate that incorporating thermal awareness into the architectural design of ImC systems is essential for achieving energy efficiency and long-term reliability.
keywords: computer architecture;microarchitecture;embedded systems;edge computing;intermittent computing;model inference;artificial intelligence

name: Biswajit Bhattacharjya
thesis_title: Magnetic Photocatalysts in Wastewater Treatment and its Recovery
abstract: The presence of pharmaceutically active compounds (PhACs) in aquatic environments has emerged as a significant environmental concern, necessitating the development of efficient and sustainable wastewater treatment technologies. Among various approaches, photocatalysis has attracted considerable attention; however, limited visible-light utilization, rapid charge-carrier recombination, and difficulties in catalyst recovery remain major challenges. Magnetic photocatalysts offer the advantage of facile separation and recovery using an external magnetic field, thereby minimizing secondary contamination. In this context, the proposed research aims to develop bioinspired magnetic photocatalysts, including Fe3O4, NiO, and Co3O4, using Mimosa pudica and Camellia sinensis extracts as natural reducing and stabilizing agents. Preliminary investigations demonstrated the successful synthesis of Mimosa pudica-mediated Fe3O4 nanoparticles with an average crystallite size of 28.30 nm, saturation magnetization of 74.77 emu/g, and a reduced optical bandgap of 1.48 eV. The material achieved 87.75% ciprofloxacin degradation under visible-light irradiation and 87.5% magnetic recovery after five reuse cycles. Building on these findings, the study will investigate transition metal and gadolinium doping, Fe3O4/NiO/Co3O4 heterostructure development, and photocatalytic performance under visible irradiation. Furthermore, laboratory and pilot-scale experiments, followed by continuous-flow reactor development, will be undertaken to establish an efficient and recoverable wastewater treatment system.
keywords: Pharmaceutical Active Compounds; Bio-based magnetic photocatalysts; Catalyst recovery; Ecotoxicity analysis

name: AMIT KUMAR CHAURASIYA
thesis_title: Deep Learning-Driven Design and Biomechanical Optimization of Patient-Specific PEEK Cranial Implants
abstract: Cranial defects resulting from trauma, tumour resection, or decompressive surgery require implants that restore protection, symmetry, and mechanical integrity. Conventional titanium and PMMA implants are often limited by stress shielding, imaging artefacts, poor patient-specific fit, or insufficient strength. Polyetheretherketone (PEEK), a high-performance, radiolucent polymer with bone-like stiffness, is a promising alternative, particularly when patient-specific implants are produced via additive manufacturing. This research develops an integrated workflow for the design and biomechanical optimization of patient-specific PEEK cranial implants. Computed tomography data are segmented using U-Net-family deep learning models, with Attention U-Net giving the best performance, and the segmented skull is reconstructed into three-dimensional models using Marching Cubes. Implant geometries are then designed to match the patient’s cranial curvature, overcoming the limitations of conventional geometric hole-filling methods. Finite element analysis under physiological and impact loading evaluates stress and deformation, and structural and fixation-location optimization is applied to ensure mechanical adequacy. The structural performance of PEEK is compared with titanium and PMMA to establish its suitability as the primary implant material. Overall, the work aims to provide a systematic, patient-specific, and mechanically validated approach to cranial implant design that supports safer, better-fitting reconstruction and future clinical translation.
keywords: Deep Learning Segmentation; Patient-Specific Implant; Cranioplasty; Medical Image Segmentation; Computed Tomography; Fixation Optimization; Biomechanical Optimization; 3D Reconstruction; Additive manufacturing

name: SHASHI BHUSHAN SINGH
thesis_title: Structure-Property-Performance Relationships in Engineered Cerium-Based Metal-Organic Framework for Heavy Metals Remediation
abstract: The research investigates the rational design and engineering of cerium-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for the remediation of heavy-metal-contaminated aqueous environments. MOF-808(Ce) was systematically modified through post-synthetic ligand functionalization using nitrogen-, oxygen-, and sulfur-containing functionalities, metal-node engineering through Ce/Mo bimetallic integration, and composite fabrication with zeolite. The developed adsorbents were evaluated for adsorption performance, metal-ion selectivity, competitive adsorption, regeneration, and applicability in different water matrices. Comprehensive investigations of adsorption kinetics, equilibrium isotherms, and thermodynamics were undertaken to elucidate adsorption behaviour and underlying structure–property relationships. Response surface methodology (RSM) was employed for process optimization, while density functional theory (DFT) was incorporated to investigate molecular-level interactions and adsorption mechanisms. Artificial neural network (ANN) modelling was explored for predictive analysis of adsorption performance. Furthermore, MOF–zeolite composites were immobilized in alginate matrices and evaluated under continuous-flow fixed-bed column conditions using established breakthrough models. Spectroscopic and physicochemical characterization provided insights into metal coordination, surface complexation, and ion-exchange mechanisms. Overall, this work integrates functional material synthesis, computational chemistry, statistical optimization, machine-learning-based prediction, and adsorption process engineering to advance multifunctional MOF-based materials for sustainable water treatment.

name: Sonagara Abhishek Maganbhai
thesis_title: Antennas based on SSPP for B5G Radio Stripe Network application
abstract:
The deployment of Beyond 5G (B5G) networks relies on advanced architectures like cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) systems to ensure ubiquitous, high-capacity connectivity. A highly practical implementation approach for this is the B5G radio stripe network (RSN). This thesis presents the design, development, and experimental validation of low-cost, low-profile, and flexible microwave passive devices, specifically focusing on antennas based on spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) structures. 
By leveraging uniplanar SSPP technology, the proposed designs achieve tight electromagnetic field confinement, enabling ultra-thin, highly efficient radiation characteristics suitable for conformal mounting. The research details the development of novel flexible endfire MIMO antennas and filtennas optimized for RSNs with circuit modelling. To validate their real-world applicability, the fabricated devices were rigorously measured over different surfaces, such as flat and curved brick walls and wood. 
The experimental results demonstrate that the SSPP-based antennas maintain robust impedance matching, stable radiation patterns, and high port isolation even under structural bending conditions. Ultimately, this work provides a scalable, resilient, and cost-effective physical layer solution, significantly advancing the practical deployment of flexible antenna systems for next-generation B5G radio stripe networks.
keywords: Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton (SSPP); Beyond 5G (B5G) Radio Stripe Network (RSN); Cell-Free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO); Uniplanar Flexible Antennas; Circuit modelling of SSPP unit cell; Endfire MIMO Antennas

name: Devendra Kumar
thesis_title: Multifunctional grid connected converter using model predictive control
abstract: The rapid integration of renewable energy resources (RESs) and electric vehicle (EV) charging stations is transforming distribution grids, requiring advanced power electronic converters and control strategies to maintain voltage and current quality within grid-code limits. To address these challenges, unified power quality conditioners (UPQCs) are utilized to form meshed hybrid microgrids by extending the UPQC DC link into a low-voltage DC (LVDC) line parallel to existing AC lines. This configuration enhances power management, accommodates new DC loads, and ensures reliable operation during grid voltage sags. Additionally, dynamic voltage control maximizes the utilization of the UPQC’s series converter to maintain grid-code voltage profiles under extreme load and generation conditions. For energy storage and EV charging applications, finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) is applied to bi-directional DC-DC converters to regulate DC bus voltage and manage battery charging via constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) modes. Finally, FCS-MPC is further leveraged in isolated three-phase four-wire grid-forming converters to supply balanced, unbalanced, and non-linear loads via a single voltage-regulation loop, as well as in droop-controlled solar PV-battery hybrid systems to dynamically regulate DC bus voltage based on battery state of charge (SoC) and load variations.
keywords: Battery energy storage system; bi-directional DC-DC converter; electric vehicle (EV) charging; finite control set model predictive control; grid-forming converter; power quality; renewable energy resources (RESs); unified power quality conditioner (UPQC).

name: Joyshree Chakraborty
discipline: Centre for Linguistic Science and Technology
thesis_title: Detecting L2 Hindi: The Case of Assamese Speakers Speaking Hindi
abstract:
This research focuses on developing robust and inclusive speech technologies through Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Natural Language Processing (NLP), with particular emphasis on accented speech recognition and computational speech analysis. The study investigates the influence of Assamese (L1) on Hindi (L2) and its implications for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems.
Key contributions include developing speech datasets, including a spontaneous Assamese-accented Hindi corpus comprising 103 speakers, and designing computational frameworks for accent identification and speech analysis. By fine-tuning a pretrained Wav2Vec2 model, the research reduced Word Error Rate (WER) from 30.15% to 6.88%, demonstrating effective adaptation of deep learning models to accented speech.
The work further explores acoustic feature extraction, prosodic modeling, Rhythm Formant Analysis (RFA), and machine learning classifiers. Combining MFCC and RFA features with Support Vector Machines achieved 76% accuracy in three-class accent classification. Additionally, latent speech embeddings were investigated to identify language-specific prosodic characteristics, alongside the deployment of a web-based accent identification system. Overall, this research demonstrates practical expertise in speech AI, data-driven modeling, transfer learning, feature engineering, model evaluation, and deployment, contributing to multilingual speech technologies and real-world AI applications.
keywords: Artificial Intelligence (AI); Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Natural Language Processing (NLP); Speech Processing; Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR); Self-Supervised Learning; Wav2Vec2; Transfer Learning; Accent Classification; Acoustic Feature Engineering; Cross Linguistic Influence; First Language Influence on Second Language; Multilingual Speech Technology

name: RAMESH OJHA
thesis_title: On Some Numerical and Data-Driven Approach for Options Pricing
abstract: This research develops accurate and computationally efficient numerical methods for pricing European and American options under realistic volatility models. For European options, a fourth order collocation method provides accurate spatial approximations, while its spline representation facilitates calculation of option sensitivities, known as Greeks. For American options, a second order collocation framework incorporates early exercise constraints through a free boundary problem formulated as a variational inequality or linear complementarity problem. Ongoing empirical research collects, processes, and analyzes United States market option data across multiple underlying stocks, strike prices, and maturities. Numerical prices will be compared with market quotations and established benchmarks using suitable pricing error measures to evaluate accuracy and practical applicability. In parallel, neural network approaches are being developed to investigate further improvements in pricing accuracy and computational efficiency. Planned research includes high order finite element methods for European and American options under the Constant Elasticity of Variance model, emphasizing convergence, numerical stability, Greeks, and optimal exercise boundaries. Subsequent work will extend the framework to the Heston stochastic volatility model and associated higher dimensional pricing problems. Ultimately, the study aims to integrate rigorous numerical analysis with data driven learning for efficient option pricing, reliable sensitivity computation, and potential model calibration.
keywords: Option Pricing; Local Volatility; European and American Options; Collocation Method; Finite Element Method; CEV Model; Heston Model; Machine Learning; Financial Market Data.

name: Rajarshi Saha
abstract: Dual active bridge (DAB) is a  DC-DC converter. It provides galvanic isolation and bidirectional power flow. Dual phase-shift (DPS) modulation combines internal and external phase-shift in DAB. So, DPS provides 2 degree freedom of power flow. For a given power level, many combinations of phase-shift ratios are possible in DPS of DAB. In input parallel output parallel (IPOP) converter, multiple DABs are connected in input parallel output parallel mode. In IPOP, currents are distributed among all DABs and switching stress is reduced. So, in low voltage high power applications IPOP is suitable. In EV fast charging applications, high power is needed. So, IPOP is more advantageous than other DC-DC converters in EV application. Also high efficient power is needed in EV charging station. So, initially for each DAB using dual phase-shift (DPS) modulation at a given power level efficiency is optimized using Lagrange multiplier and the theoretical analysis is verified by  MATLAB simulation and experiments on laboratory prototype. Then in IPOP, efficiency is optimized at a given power level and it is verified in MATLAB simulink. In future the analysis is needed to be verified in hardware prototype.
keywords: Dual Active Bridge; Dual Phase-Shift; Efficiency Optimization; Input Parallel Output Parallel Converters

name: MUKESH BHARTI
thesis_title: Development and Performance Evaluation of a Rotating-Anode Electrocoagulation System with Hybrid Electrodes for the Treatment of Arsenic- and Fluoride-Contaminated Groundwater and Ni–Co–Mn-Bearing Wastewater
abstract: Arsenic and fluoride contamination of groundwater is a serious public health concern, particularly in rural India, while industrial effluents containing nickel, cobalt, and manganese pose additional environmental risks. Conventional treatment methods often require high chemical consumption, produce large sludge volumes, and are poorly suited for decentralized use. This research presents the design, development, and performance evaluation of a rotating-anode electrocoagulation system with hybrid electrodes for treating arsenic- and fluoride-contaminated groundwater and Ni–Co–Mn-bearing wastewater. In this system, coagulants are generated in situ by electrochemical dissolution of the anode, eliminating the need for external chemical dosing, while anode rotation is intended to improve mass transfer and contaminant removal. The effects of key operating parameters, including current density, inter-electrode distance, rotational speed, treatment time, pH, and electrode geometry, were systematically investigated to identify optimal conditions. Reaction kinetics, energy consumption, and techno-economic feasibility were evaluated for simultaneous arsenate and fluoride removal. Supporting analyses using ICP-MS, ion chromatography, FTIR, XRD, FESEM-EDX, and BET characterization were conducted to elucidate the removal mechanisms. The results establish rotating-anode electrocoagulation as a promising, low-cost technology for producing safe drinking water and treating heavy-metal-bearing industrial wastewater, with strong potential for community-scale implementation.
keywords: Electrocoagulation; Rotating Anode; Arsenic Removal; Fluoride Removal; Heavy Metal Wastewater Treatment; Techno-Economic Evaluation
